title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: admins create custom MCP connectors in the admin centre
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, licensing, controls and descriptions of user-approved actions are supported. Minor corrections should identify the deciding request properties in the automation rows and acknowledge two further inconsistencies between Microsoft's overview, prerequisites and custom setup documentation.

claims.claim: Admins can create custom MCP connectors in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Admins can create custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors in the Microsoft 365 Admin Centre and deploy them across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes deploying the connectors across Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Admins can create custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) connectors in the Microsoft 365 Admin Centre and deploy them across Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: The roadmap says these connectors surface an organisation's custom data in Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This will allow admins to surface their organization's custom data in Microsoft 365 Copilot via these MCP-based connectors.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The roadmap target is February CY2026.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "February CY2026"

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Preview and Targeted Release.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": [ "Preview", "Targeted Release" ]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": [ "Web" ]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), not GCC, GCC High or DoD.
claims.quote: "clouds": [ "Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)" ]

claims.claim: The roadmap supplies no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Custom connector creation is admin-opt-in: an admin must create and configure the connector.
claims.quote: After you set up authentication, create the connector in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature is included within the Microsoft 365 Copilot entitlement rather than separately licensed.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.claim: Learn documents custom federated connectors connecting an MCP server's tools to Copilot for internal data access or actions.
claims.quote: A custom federated connector starts with a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that exposes tools for Microsoft 365 Copilot to access data or take actions in your internal systems.
claims.fix: After the sentence identifying custom federated connectors, add: 'The general Copilot connectors overview still marks Custom connectors as No in its Federated connectors column, unlike the dedicated custom setup page.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/overview#types-of-copilot-connectors, whose table reads 'Custom connectors | Yes | No | No'.

claims.where: summary; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The custom setup page specifies Global Administrator or AI Administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Global Administrator or AI Administrator role in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Creation follows Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > Created by your org > Create a new connector > Add > Custom connector > Connect to MCP server > Add.
claims.quote: Under Created by your org, find the Create a new connector tile and select Add. On the Custom connector page, under Connect to MCP server, select Add.

claims.claim: The creation form takes a display name, description and MCP server base URL, and Save creates the connector.
claims.quote: Display name | The user-facing name for your connector. ... Description | A summary of your data source and the information it provides. ... Base URL | Your MCP server endpoint. ... Select Save to create the connector.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Entra SSO uses a Teams Developer Portal SSO registration ID entered during connector setup.
claims.quote: For Microsoft Entra SSO, enter the SSO registration ID from the Teams Developer Portal.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: OAuth 2.0 uses a Teams Developer Portal OAuth registration ID entered during connector setup.
claims.quote: For OAuth 2.0, enter the OAuth registration ID from the Teams Developer Portal.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Custom federated connectors support Microsoft Entra SSO, OAuth 2.0 and No Auth.
claims.quote: Custom federated connectors support three authentication methods. ... Microsoft Entra SSO ... OAuth 2.0 ... No Auth
claims.fix: After listing the authentication methods, add: 'The general connectors prerequisites page instead lists an OAuth-based identity configuration as a federated prerequisite; the custom setup page explicitly also supports No Auth.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites, which requires 'An OAuth-based identity configuration between the external service and Microsoft Entra ID'.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: No Auth requires neither user authentication nor authentication setup.
claims.quote: No Auth | Users don't need to authenticate. | None

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Federated connectors do not index external data into Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Don't index external data into Microsoft 365.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Connector actions execute in the connected service on the user's behalf.
claims.quote: Actions run in the third-party service on behalf of the user and are limited by that user's permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure and Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The source system's user permissions govern what data and actions the connector can access.
claims.quote: The authenticated user's identity and permissions in the source system govern tool access. Users can only access information they're authorized to view and change data they're authorized to modify.

claims.claim: Data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements. Review the terms provided by non-Microsoft agent and plugin publishers

claims.claim: An MCP server restricting incoming traffic by IP must allow Microsoft's static egress addresses.
claims.quote: If your MCP server restricts incoming traffic by source IP address, allow the static egress IP addresses used by Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Static egress is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Static egress is enabled by default; no manifest flag is required.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Create, update and delete tools initially require explicit user approval.
claims.quote: Tools that create, update, or delete data initially require the user's explicit approval.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Allow for conversation suppresses further approval requests for that tool during the current conversation.
claims.quote: Allow for conversation | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool for the rest of the current conversation.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Always allow permits subsequent calls without asking again.
claims.quote: Always allow | Runs the action and doesn't ask again for this tool until the user changes the setting or the publisher changes the tool.

claims.claim: Persisted approval applies to an individual tool rather than the whole connector.
claims.quote: Always allow and Allow for conversation apply to the individual tool, not to the whole connector.

claims.claim: Write, update and delete tools are included in the connector and not enabled separately.
claims.quote: Write, update, and delete tools are part of the connector and aren't enabled separately.

claims.claim: The general overview still calls federated connectors read-only, unlike the dedicated overview's write documentation.
claims.quote: Write actions will be available starting early October 2026. ... Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn labels the admin-center connector tools view as coming soon.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)

claims.claim: Connector setting changes can take up to 10 minutes to reach Microsoft 365 experiences.
claims.quote: Changes can take up to 10 minutes to take effect across Microsoft 365 experiences.

claims.claim: Users may need to refresh Copilot or start a new conversation after a change.
claims.quote: Users might need to refresh Copilot or start a new conversation.

claims.claim: Delete permanently removes the custom connector and configuration and cannot be undone.
claims.quote: Delete permanently removes a custom connector and its configuration. You can't undo it.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[2].note; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Disable pauses the connector while preserving its configuration.
claims.quote: Disable ... pauses the connector without removing its configuration. You can enable it again.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Federated connectors require Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licensing or Microsoft 365 E7 for the tenant and users.
claims.quote: Federated Copilot connectors are available only to tenants and users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license (or Microsoft 365 E7).

claims.claim: The prerequisites list the Copilot add-on for every user querying the federated source.
claims.quote: A Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license for every user who queries the federated source.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio licences do not support federated connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go does not support federated connectors.
claims.quote: They aren't supported with Copilot Studio licenses or Microsoft 365 Copilot pay-as-you-go.

claims.claim: With Microsoft 365 Copilot licences, connector grounding is included without extra charges.
claims.quote: If your organization has Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, connector grounding in Copilot is included, and no extra charges apply.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A price or credit rate specific to custom MCP connectors is not published as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: custom MCP federated connectors price credit rate billing license. Opened connectors prerequisites, custom setup and federated overview; no custom connector rate. Results on ERP MCP and Azure Connector Namespace meter different services.

claims.claim: The custom setup prerequisites include an appropriate Microsoft Entra admin role for SSO.
claims.quote: An appropriate Microsoft Entra admin role for single sign-on (SSO) authentication.

claims.claim: The custom setup prerequisites include access to the Teams Developer Portal.
claims.quote: Access to the Teams Developer Portal.

claims.claim: The managing-availability page lists Global Administrator and Search Administrator as alternative roles.
claims.quote: To manage federated connectors, you need one of the following administrator roles: Global Administrator; Search Administrator

claims.claim: The general connectors prerequisites page instead requires an AI administrator for configuration and deployment.
claims.quote: To configure and deploy Copilot connectors, you must be an AI administrator in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Admins can see all connectors in Your connections even when they are unavailable to users.
claims.quote: Admins can see every connector in Your connections for governance, even when it's disabled, blocked, staged to No users, or its type is cleared in Agent and plugin access.

claims.where: summary; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users must be included in User access to use a custom federated connector.
claims.quote: Does the User access setting apply to federated connectors? Yes, including connectors delivered as Microsoft 365 app packages.

claims.where: summary; Scope; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Users must also fall within the connector's staged audience.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user is included in the connector's staged rollout.

claims.claim: Connector availability also requires it to be enabled and not blocked.
claims.quote: The connector is enabled and not blocked in Agents > Tools.

claims.claim: A non-admin test user can check effective connector availability in Copilot Chat > Settings > Sources.
claims.quote: Then sign in as a test user who isn't an admin, open Copilot Chat > Settings > Sources, and confirm the connector isn't listed.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Organisation-built availability is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access > Allow agents and plugins built by your organization.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access. ... Allow agents and plugins built by your organization (custom connectors)

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply organisation-built availability through preview TCM applyOnce.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors ... mode ... monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue
claims.fix: Append to controls[0].note and the matching rendered note: 'Set mode=applyOnce and baseline.resources[].resourceType=microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes, resourceVersion=1, with properties.valueObject.areTenantScopedAppsAllowed=false.' The property is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources; the body already describes it, but the row's note does not.

claims.claim: The organisation-built availability setting is a tenant-level control governing custom MCP connectors.
claims.quote: The Allow agents and plugins built by your organization setting in Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access governs custom connectors.

claims.claim: Clearing a publisher type sets its existing connectors' staged rollout to No users.
claims.quote: When you clear an option, existing connectors of that type remain visible to admins ... but their staged rollout is set to No users.

claims.claim: An individual connector setting takes precedence over bulk publisher-type availability.
claims.quote: A setting you make on an individual connector takes precedence over the bulk Agent and plugin access setting. User access always applies.

claims.claim: Tenant-wide User access is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Settings > User access.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can set User access through preview TCM applyOnce.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... POST /admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors
claims.fix: Append to controls[1].note and the matching rendered note: 'Set mode=applyOnce and baseline.resources[].resourceType=microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion=1, with properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory=everyone or noOne.' The property is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/utcm-agent-resources; the row currently gives the values without naming it.

claims.claim: User access offers All users (the default), Specific users or groups, and No users.
claims.quote: All users - This option is the default. ... No users ... Specific users or groups

claims.claim: User access sets the maximum population, which connector staging can narrow but cannot widen.
claims.quote: Only these users can use any connector. Connector staging can narrow but not widen this population.

claims.claim: Individual group or user staging is at Copilot > Connectors > Your connections > connector > Staged rollout.
claims.quote: After you create a connector, it appears in the Your Connections list. ... Select your connector. Select Staged rollout. Choose Users or Groups.

claims.claim: Automation for individual custom-connector staging is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: graph custom federated connector staged rollout users groups API block connector. Opened custom setup, manage availability and Graph TCM Agent schemas; read staged-rollout search excerpt. No staging API found; TCM lists publisher types, sharing and useraccess.

claims.claim: Enable makes the connector available to its staged audience within User access.
claims.quote: Enable | Makes the connector available to its staged audience, within the users allowed by User access.

claims.where: controls[3].ui; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: A connector can be blocked in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Agents > Tools > connector > Block.
claims.quote: Block (Agents > Tools) | Same as Disable. ... Agents > Tools: Block or unblock connectors and tools.

claims.claim: Automation for individual custom-connector blocking is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: graph custom federated connector staged rollout users groups API block connector. Opened custom setup, manage availability and Graph TCM Agent schemas. Found UI blocking and bulk publisher-type automation, but no API for individual custom connector blocking.

claims.claim: Block under Agents > Tools has the same effect as Disable.
claims.quote: Block (Agents > Tools) has the same effect as Disable.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Deploy to all users remains limited to the population included in User access.
claims.quote: Deploy to all users makes the connector available to everyone included in User access

claims.claim: TCM remediation and applyOnce are preview capabilities available through Microsoft Graph beta.
claims.quote: These capabilities are available in preview through Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: The allowedagenttypes baseline uses resourceType=microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes, resourceVersion=1 and properties.valueObject.areTenantScopedAppsAllowed=false to disallow organisation-built items.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.agent.allowedagenttypes", "resourceVersion": 1 ... "properties": { "valueObject": { ... "areTenantScopedAppsAllowed": true ... } }; areTenantScopedAppsAllowed ... Indicates whether apps, agents, and plugins built by the organization are allowed.

claims.claim: The useraccess baseline uses resourceType=microsoft.agent.useraccess, resourceVersion=1 and properties.valueObject.userAssignmentCategory=everyone or noOne.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.agent.useraccess", "resourceVersion": 1 ... "properties": { "valueObject": { "userAssignmentCategory": "everyone" } }; userAssignmentCategory ... Allowed Values ... everyone, noOne

claims.claim: The TCM useraccess schema does not document assigning specific users or groups.
claims.quote: Searched: graph utcm agent useraccess specific users groups userAssignmentCategory. Opened the full TCM Agent resources page; AgentUserAccessValueObject lists only userAssignmentCategory with everyone and noOne. No user or group assignment property is documented.

claims.claim: Creating an applyOnce monitor requires delegated rather than application access.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only.

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the documented signed-in user role for applying the two Agent settings through TCM.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user.

claims.claim: Learn says TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.
claims.quote: TCM is available only in the global service, not in national clouds.

claims.claim: TCM can apply the supplied baseline once by creating a monitor with mode=applyOnce and an inline baseline.
claims.quote: baseline ... Required for an inline-baseline monitor. ... mode ... The possible values are: monitorOnly, applyOnce, unknownFutureValue. ... An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The federated connectors overview says admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview, without the briefing asserting any particular audit event.
claims.quote: Can read data and, where a connector provides the tools, create, update, or delete data with the user's approval. Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.
